title: Calendula eyewash for conjunctivitis
subtitle: A sterile calendula infusion for external eye irrigation in mild non-infectious conjunctivitis
excerpt: Calendula eyewash is a precisely cooled, freshly prepared infusion of dried Calendula officinalis flowers, filtered through doubled muslin to remove all particles, and used as an external wash for mild non-infectious conjunctivitis, the sore, gritty, irritated eyes of hay fever or environmental irritation. Sterile preparation is mandatory; contaminated eyewash causes infection. Prepared fresh for each use. Not for children, not for bacterial or viral conjunctivitis.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), calendula entry, Botanical.com. EMA HMPC Community herbal monograph on Calendula officinalis L., flos (2008, revised 2020), open access. External ocular use of calendula: traditional European practice documented in 19th-century pharmacopoeias.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare fresh for each use. Never store prepared eyewash, contamination risk.

glossaryTerms.definition: A small cup or bowl designed to hold liquid against the eye socket so the open eye can be bathed in solution. Used to wash the conjunctival surface gently. Available from pharmacies; wash thoroughly with boiling water before and after each use.

content.text: Calendula eyewash is a freshly prepared infusion of dried calendula flowers, filtered through doubled muslin and cooled to body temperature. Used as an external
for hay fever eye symptoms: watery, itchy, gritty, or sticky eyes. Also used for eye soreness from dust or smoke. Sterile preparation is essential. Any contaminated liquid can cause infection.

attrs.title: Precautions, read carefully before making eye preparations
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

items.prepNote: freshly boiled water, must be boiling to sterilise

content.text: Wash your hands. Rinse the eye bath and a small jug with boiling water. Place 1 teaspoon of dried calendula in a clean cup.
Pour 200 ml of freshly boiled water over the flowers. Cover and steep for 10 minutes.
Strain through doubled clean muslin into the rinsed jug, pressing the flowers. Re-strain through the doubled muslin a second time to ensure no flower particles remain.
Allow to cool to body temperature, test by dripping a small amount on the inner wrist. It should feel neither warm nor cold. Never use if still warm. never use refrigerated liquid.
Fill the eye bath with the cooled solution. Lean forward, press the eye bath to the eye socket, and tilt back to bathe the open eye for 30,60 seconds. Repeat for the second eye with fresh solution.
Once or twice daily during hay fever season for allergic eye irritation. Prepare fresh for each session.
Prepare fresh for each session. Discard any unused solution immediately.
When not to use this remedy

Do not use for suspected bacterial or viral conjunctivitis, eye pain, vision change, or photophobia. See a doctor or optometrist for any eye symptom that is new, worsening, or comes with discharge, crusting, or significant redness.
